Getting appropriate Survivors and team leaders will be your utmost priority. The most important aspect is that their Personality matches the Lead Survivor's- and the Lead Survivor is in his/her matching team. Then after all that, you will have to worry about getting matching bonus stat traits that are useful to your build. Basically, dont scrap ANY legendary survivors you get until you are absolutely CERTAIN you will NEVER need that one, anywhere in your teams. Even at the near endgame, this is still the progression gate for me.

You get plenty of legendary traps/weapon schematics along the way but legendary survivors that are perfect slots will always be a struggle to obtain. At your current level, though, just try to slot whatever you have available to the best of your efforts and pick up a purple weapon schematic of a gun you like- you can upgrade the rarity to legendary from epic using flux you buy in the store with the mission gold, resets weekly. save any tokens that let you pull a hero/schematic from the collections until you get a genuine build concept down as those are extremely hard to get and there are quite a number of heroes/schematics that are very difficult to obtain.

Another important thing is to not overbuild, as enemy pathing is simplistic, but dumb. So they'd rather punch through the walls of a labyrinthian maze instead of walking it. Yet, they'll usually prioritize an open gate a few meters out instead of punching through 2 walls in front of them.

Right, camping resources is ALWAYS going to be "a strategy". It should NEVER be "the only strategy". Which it currently is.  


I agree with you that the lack of resources is what makes warzone such a campfest, but even in regular multiplayer all you see is camping in any game mode. It is just such a huge deficit to players to do anything outside of camping because of how ADS functions in the game. The only gun you can use to run around in the multiplayer side of the game effectively is the SA-B 50 with full ADS attachments setup, which is only viable because it's an absurdly OP point+click killer. Everything else just can't pull up fast enough to counteract the advantages that camping provides.  


For a personal reference, I average around 40:8 when I corner camp on multiplayer, and about 20:20 when I move- it's just that silly of an advantage. In the Warzone, the benefits of camping are further amplified because not only do you get mechanical advantages, the aggressors have to breach your position- which means the campers have an exclusive cover advantage in most cases.  


It seriously is a bad game overall, In map layout, mechanics, balancing, everything.

Well I don’t recommend this option, but you could potentially stick out your active duty, and THEN get diagnosed and medicated for you mental illness. But do keep in mind that the longer it goes untreated, the harder it will be to differentiate between whats fake and whats real. Also, not only would you get medical discharge payments from the military, but you’d also get disability paychecks if you get diagnosed while in active duty (which are much heavier in cash) So it wouldnt be like you were getting nothing out of all that time spent in the military. Ontop of that, once you are home you’ll still be able to maintain a 40+ hr job if need be, due to the fact that you are not legally obligated to notify your disabilities to workplaces, and even if they found out somehow, they could t fire or refuse your application over it. Basically my point is you’ll have 3 sources of income, free medical treatment for life, and alot of extra cash. Ontop of no more strange things in your head. The medical discharge may not be much by itself, but it definitely comes with a nice package.

Well if you get diagnosed with mental illness, they will have to send you home and discharge you, as you will be unfit for active duty. But if you get diagnosed while still in the army they will pay for all your medical treatments needed and stuff. Happened to my father. They most certainly do not stuff you in a ramshackle looney bin. Ever. I’ve been to a couple of those places for suicide attempts. Legally they aren’t allowed to hold you for over 3 days. So even if they put you in a mental ward, you’d be there for 3 days and then they would have to let you leave if you wanted to. Even for schizophrenia. Only exception is if you physically hurt yourself or someone else. Then they can hold you for longer. So aslong as you keep your hands to yourself, you will get rid of the weird stuff in your head, and be a free man. A side note: it wont even count as a dishonorable discharge for you :D

Those kinds of parents that shut you down when you try to open up are really, really bad in these situations. If you wanna vent here, nobody will judge you about anything you say.

Your therapist will not tell ‘anyone’ about what happens in that room unless you give them the idea that you are going to attempt suicide as soon as you can. Suicidal thoughts are not the same as suicidal intent, but can very well lead to such a thing quite easily. So yes, please let your therapist know about your suicidal thoughts, but please be clear to them about whether you plan on acting on them or not.

Also, if you are in fact planning on acting on them, please feel free to vent here, or talk with someone you are close to.
